## Problem

Design a system that a library can use to manage its book collection and lending. The system must provide the following capabilities:

1. Register a new book in the catalog, capturing its title, its author, and its ISBN.
2. Look up books using any one of three keys: title, author, or ISBN.
3. Lend a book to a patron, storing who borrowed it and the date the loan began.
4. Track books that are currently on loan: let users see the lending status of a book, and process the return of a borrowed book.

Your deliverables are the data model (database schema) and the API architecture for this system. In your design, address how the system scales as the catalog and the number of users grow, and explain how you handle locking of shared resources (for example, preventing conflicting operations on the same book).

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Identify the core entities (book, patron, loan) and notice that a loan is a relationship with its own dates, not just a flag on a book.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Design tables for books and loans with indexes on title, author and ISBN for lookup, and expose REST-style endpoints for adding books, searching, lending and returning.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Think about multiple copies of the same ISBN, preventing a book from being lent twice at once, and how return updates the loan record while keeping history.

</details>
